observations: Photo 0 and 1 show a retail box for a Kzubr brand PPR pipe welding machine.
The box specifies model KPPR-1600 and 1600 Watts power.
Photo 2 shows an open orange metal carry case containing the welding tool.
The tool has a data plate matching the box: Kzubr KPPR-1600.
Accessories visible include six welding dies (sockets), a pair of gloves, a tape measure, an Allen key, a manual, and a pipe cutter in bubble wrap.
The photos contain watermarks 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'EZE TOOLS'.

claims.evidence: Photos 0, 1, and 2 clearly show the brand is Kzubr, not IFAN.

claims.claim: uses to join two or more pieces of plastic pipes
claims.evidence: This is the standard function of a PPR welding machine as shown in the photos.

risks.proof: A video showing the device plugged in, heating up, and the indicator lights functioning.

risks.risk: Worn or damaged non-stick coating on welding dies
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the interior and exterior surfaces of the black welding sockets.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring a full set of replacement dies

risks.risk: Damaged or dull pipe cutter blade
risks.proof: Photo of the pipe cutter removed from the bubble wrap showing the blade edge.

proof_requests: Video of the machine powered on and reaching welding temperature.
Close-up photos of the welding dies to check the teflon coating.
Photo of the pipe cutter out of its bubble wrap.
response.reason: The item is clearly identified by brand and model from the photos. Although the seller's text misidentifies the brand as IFAN, the visual evidence of the Kzubr KPPR-1600 is consistent across all images, allowing for a worst-case valuation.
